name: MA-06
label: Safe D

Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near certain to win

model.rationale: The D+11 lean, a favorable environment, and Koh's lopsided fundraising edge point to a Democratic margin near twenty points, and prediction markets price Democrats near certain to hold the open seat. No public polls contest that picture, so fundamentals carry the forecast.
model.watch: Published general-election polling or a late wave of outside spending on Jones's behalf would be the clearest signs the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Seth Moulton's Senate run leaves this D+11 district north of Boston open, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic territory amid a favorable national climate. Dan Koh has built a commanding financial position, raising more than $4.7 million and holding roughly $2 million on hand, while outside groups have spent over $1.7 million supporting him and nothing is recorded against his side. Republican Micah Jones has raised under $600,000 with about $215,000 available, far short of the resources needed to compete here.

Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near certain to hold the seat, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. No general-election polls have been published, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and the political environment rather than direct survey data.
